newsitem.title: USA: Albright to meet Hong Kong's Lee on Monday.
newsitem.headline: Albright to meet Hong Kong's Lee on Monday.

text.p: U.S. Secretary of State Madeleine Albright will meet Martin Lee, the leader of Hong Kong's democracy movement on Monday, and may travel to the British colony, U.S. officials said on Friday.

In a move that would provide an opportunity to show U.S. support for political freedoms in Hong Kong, Albright is seriously considering a joint British-Chinese invitation to attend the festivities when the British colony is returned to Chinese rule on July 1, administration officials told Reuters.

In the meeting with Lee, Albright will discuss issues related to Hong Kong's reversion to China's control, including protection of civil liberties and fundamental freedoms of the rule of law, "which are very important," State Department spokesman Nicholas Burns said.
Lee is on a lobbying mission in the United States ahead of the switchover, amid concern over indications that China wants to tighten controls on political and civil liberties.
Hong Kong's future leader Tung Chee-hwa on Wednesday made a proposal to curtail protests and foreign funding for political parties in the British colony after it reverts to Chinese rule.
The White House said on Thursday it was "fundamentally important" that Hong Kong residents continue to enjoy the freedoms they now have when China takes over.
Republican Sen. Jesse Helms, chairman of the Senate Foreign Relations Committee, has urged that President Bill Clinton also receive Lee, but the White House has not indicated whether he will.
Burns said Albright had been formally invited to the festivities surrounding the switchover from British to Chinese rule but had not decided whether to accept.
Another U.S. official said the secretary was "seriously considering" the invitation and was expected to accept it, especially since it came from close U.S. ally Britain, as well as China.
